statement: The pinned WiiBrew MotionPlus page describes six-byte data alternating between gyro records and downstream extension records during pass-through. For Nunchuk mode 0x05, its downstream report loses one low bit on each of the three acceleration axes; the final two bytes reassign the upper bits originally used for its C/Z buttons and accelerometer fragments: the original byte-5 bit 7 takes bit 6, original byte-4 bit 0 takes byte-5 bit 7, byte-5 bit 3 takes bit 4, bit 1 takes bit 3 and bit 0 takes bit 2, overwriting previous occupants as documented. For Classic mode 0x07, the left stick X/Y low bits are discarded, byte-4 bit 0 is overwritten and the original byte-5 bits 0 and 1 move into bit 0 of bytes 0 and 1 respectively. In both pass-through formats, byte 5 bit 1 distinguishes a gyro report (one) from an extension report (zero). This is a documentary bit mapping, not a capture or universal third-party transform.
